about: The public contract of the decode tool as MDD-071 completes it: what a request may say, in which unit each number is, what each mode shows, how pages end, which refusals exist, and what a text is not. The published input and output schemas are the reference's (conformance/manifests/tools-and-options.json) and are unchanged; everything this file adds is an additional key of an answer.

class object.truncated: the class text is one page of max_lines lines and is not continued (offset belongs to a method): true says the text has more lines than were shown; the fields and annotations are also rows of the SQL relations

method row.continuation: next_offset null: the text ends with this page. Otherwise decode the same method (file_id and method_idx) with offset = next_offset.
method row.omitted: present only when the text leaves something out: debug_events_not_at_an_instruction, positions_not_source_lines, parameter_annotation_slots_unplaced, annotation_layer_missing. What a text leaves out is never silent.
method row.summary: no text keys; registers, code_units and try_count are null for a method without a body (abstract, native), never 0

answer.next_method_offset: null on the last page, else method_offset + the number of methods shown; a method whose text the budget cut counts as shown

max_bytes.applies_to: text modes: the UTF-8 bytes of the text of the page (a method page: its text; a class page: ONE budget for all its methods' texts). summary mode of a class: the serialized bytes of the rows. 0 or a budget no character fits in is invalid_input.
max_bytes.difference: the reference counts the serialized answer and accepts only 4096..131072

method_offset.applies_to: a class selector; refused for a method (invalid_argument); past total_methods is invalid_range, equal to total_methods is an empty last page

mode.default: summary for class, smali for method

offset.applies_to: ONE method's text (smali or context); refused with a class selector (kind invalid_argument, the text of a class page continues on its method with file_id and method_idx) and with summary

timeout_ms.on expiry: deadline_exceeded and the dataset is closed

errors.when: no selector, two selectors, method_idx without file_id, an empty descriptor, an offset with a class, method_offset with a method, an offset with summary
a method or class that is not defined (or a file_id that is not in the dataset)
a descriptor defined in several DEX files and no file_id
offset or method_offset past the end, offset inside a character
max_bytes that no character fits in
the serialized answer is over the server's max_result_bytes
an argument of the wrong type, an unknown argument, max_lines or method_limit out of range

not_facts: A smali text never replaces the raw code bytes or their fingerprint: the HostLab method fingerprint is taken from the raw instruction bytes, not from this text.
The text is a display of validated facts; it is not a decompilation and states no call target, type or value that the bytes do not.
A float is shown as its shortest reading; a NaN does not keep its payload. The exact bits are the annotation facts.
A method handle is shown as method_handle_<index>; its target is a fact of the method-handle table, not text.
A debug position that is not a source line (a pc-to-pc surrogate, a non-positive line) is not written as .line.

reference_differences.why: the `error` object of every tool error carries four fields of this engine (code, stage, retryable, details) beside the reference's

the smali text follows baksmali's writing (p-registers for parameters, :cond_N/:goto_N/:try_start_N labels, .catch lines beside the code, an L on wide literals, a backslash before an apostrophe in strings); the reference writes v-registers, :label_XXXX, .catch lines at the end, no L, a bare apostrophe. The two texts are reduced to the same form (canon_smali) and must be equal: instructions, operands, literals, branch targets, payloads and exception tables. The numbers that depend on the length of the text (total_bytes, total_lines, start_line, end_line, next_offset, the mid-line flags) are compared only when the text is identical.
an error's `message` is this server's own words. Its `kind` (through KIND_ALIASES) and the file_id, method_idx and code_unit_offset it echoes are compared.

an argument of the wrong type, an unknown field, or a value outside its range (limit, max_lines, method_limit, timeout_ms) is a JSON-RPC invalid-params error here; the reference answers a tool result with isError (the serde message, or kind invalid_input).

the reference refuses max_bytes outside 4096..=131072 and timeout_ms outside 1..=60000, and `mode: null` for get_manifest; this server's max_bytes is a budget the answer must fit in (over it: quota_exceeded) and it takes `null` as the default.

a method whose invoke names a different number of registers than its prototype takes is rendered as the bytes say (the invoke is visible and wrong); the reference refuses the whole method (invalid_input, with the offset of the invoke). Showing the code of a damaged or obfuscated method is the more useful answer.
the summary mode here also names the method's `declaration`.
the xml mode of get_manifest (MDD-072) is refused as `not_implemented`; it is not compared.
every decode answer that shows text names the version of its text (`text_format`); a context row also gives `source_total_lines`, the line count of the full text its `line N:` numbers index.

a class page also carries `class`: the class's own facts (flags, superclass, source file, interfaces, field counts) and, in the text modes on the first page, its declaration, fields and annotations as a text; and a method row may carry `omitted`, what its text leaves out. The reference has neither.

the smali text here also carries annotation blocks, `.param` lines and debug directives (`.line`, `.local`, `.end local`, `.restart local`, `.prologue`, `.epilogue`, `.source`) that the reference never writes; canon_smali drops them before the texts are compared, so the instructions, operands, targets, payloads and exception tables are what is compared.

the context view keeps the same kinds of lines as the reference's (method line, registers line, label lines, catch lines; checked against the reference for every method of the fixture). Its `line N:` numbers count the lines of this server's own full text, so they are compared only through canon_context, which drops the numbers and merges the labels that name one address; the labels themselves are named by baksmali's conventions here.

in a class page `max_bytes` is one budget of UTF-8 bytes for the text of all its methods (the reference's counts the serialized answer, twice); a class page's answer is compared only where no budget is asked for.
list_tables names the 17 HostLab contract relations (as objects with name, kind and column_count) where the reference lists 56 names; list_datasets reports this server's own limits.

when a request is wrong in several ways, both engines refuse it, but the reference names the dataset first, then timeout_ms, max_bytes and the rest, and this server checks the schema of the arguments before it looks for the dataset.
a 1 ms deadline: the reference ran out of time; whether this server does depends on the clock.

selectors.ambiguity: a descriptor defined in several DEX files names none of them: kind `ambiguous`, supply file_id; the first one is never picked
selectors.file_id: names the DEX file of a method, or of a class when several files define it
selectors.only referred to: a method or class that the DEX refers to but does not define is `not_found`

text_formats.answer_key: `text_format` of the answer: the id of the text the mode shows, null for summary.

contains: 'line N: ' and the original line for the method line, register line, labels and exception-table lines (class text: class, super, source, implements and field lines)
parameter names (.param) with their annotation blocks
labels, exception table lines and instructions
class text: .class .super .source .implements, class annotations, fields with static values and field annotations

text_formats.versioning: A change to what a text says or how it is written changes its id. A change to the facts it is built from does not. mdd.smali.v1 is the first id the engine names: the text MDD-042 wrote was its instruction subset.

units.byte offset: UTF-8 bytes of ONE rendered text: offset, next_offset, total_bytes, max_bytes (and the class page's text budget)
units.code-unit address: 16-bit units of one code item: only in label names (:goto_1f is address 0x1f) and in code_units; never an offset or a line number
units.line number: lines of ONE rendered text: start_line, end_line, total_lines, max_lines; the `line N:` numbers of a context count lines of the FULL text and the context row names that count as source_total_lines
units.method offset: methods of ONE class in method_idx order: method_offset, method_limit, next_method_offset, total_methods
units.rule: No number of one unit is ever accepted or returned as another. A context's offsets page the context; the full text's offsets page the full text.
